title: Exponential-Tilt Intervention Effects with a Polynomially Vanishing Dose Edge
banked_reason: D0.5.G tier=subfield < floor=field (target=field) and NOT salvageable in scope
gap_reasons: The note proves the exact constant only within the negligible-remainder affine procedure class; for unrestricted measurable estimators it proves only a positive-constant-to-C_eta^* rate bracket on the regular-location-admissible submodel, leaving the normalized nonlinear constant and equality with C_eta^* open.

The contribution remains narrow because beta, kappa, and L are known, asymptotics are pointwise in a fixed nuisance environment, and neither confidence coverage nor adaptation or empirical validation of the sparse-edge law is delivered.

[D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 6.5 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'subfield'. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery developed the coupled contact optimizer and a sharp constant for the fixed-procedure affine class, then repaired a rowwise-infimum quantifier error and added an unrestricted critical-rate result. D0.5 graded the resulting package subfield: the unrestricted nonlinear constant, adaptation, and honest coverage remain open. The run stopped before Lean formalization under the field novelty floor.
tldr: For Schindl, Shen, and Kennedy's support-preserving exponential intervention, a polynomially vanishing dose edge creates a critical elbow: variance scale \(\delta^\beta/n\) and squared Lipschitz localization scale \(\delta^{-2}\) balance at \(\delta_n\asymp n^{1/(\beta+2)}\), giving mean squared error \(n^{-2/(\beta+2)}\). The paper derives the unique covariate-coupled contact kernel and exact constant within the fixed-procedure negligible-remainder affine class, proves uniform cross-fitted attainment including zero-contact crossings, and proves the same critical rate against every measurable estimator on the stated regular-location-admissible sparse-edge submodel. Only convergence and the exact value of the normalized nonlinear constant, including whether it equals \(C_\eta^*\), remain open.
gap: Published growing-tilt theory supplies identification, influence functions, rate bounds, and a polynomial-edge warning, while optimal-recovery theory supplies general affine principles. Neither gives the sharp covariate-coupled risk constant or a feasible uniform mean-square transfer when edge mass, variance, baseline, and active contacts are estimated.
fill: The paper solves the coupled contact program, proves a compact least-favorable affine converse, constructs clipped spline pilots, and establishes an \(o(h_n^2)\) cross-fitted remainder without excluding zero-contact boundaries.
